entries.title: Burning Steppes
body: A blackened wasteland of ash, lava and smoking craters south of Blackrock Mountain. Before the great explosion that came with Ragnaros' summoning, all of this was part of the Redridge range; now nothing grows, and the ground still burns.

This is the homeland of the Blackrock orcs, who hold a stronghold at the foot of the mountain, and of the black dragonflight, whose broodlings, drakes and dragonspawn roam the ridges. Firegut ogres guard the mines of Dreadmaul Rock for the orcs, and both the Alliance and the Horde keep small, stubborn camps here to watch them.
sources: quest 4182 description (before the great explosion, this was part of the Redridge mountain range)
pre-Cataclysm lore: the summoning of Ragnaros

entries.title: Morgan's Vigil
body: A small Alliance camp on the eastern ridge of the Burning Steppes, above the road to Redridge. Marshal Maxwell commands its soldiers, who have gathered a great deal of intelligence on the Blackrock and lost almost as many men gathering it.

Its people are worn thin. Their commanding officer, Marshal Windsor, was taken by a Blackrock raiding party along with all his documents, and Oralius, who wages a one-man war against the Firegut ogres with his imaginary friend Captain Winky, insists he is the only sane one in camp.

entries.title: Flame Crest
body: A camp on a rocky crest in the north of the Burning Steppes, overlooking the dragonkin below. Horde soldiers rest there, and a gnome named Tinkee Steamboil studies the black dragon broodlings.

Tinkee's Draco-Incarcinatrix 900 can capture a broodling's essence, and she hopes to learn to freeze dragon eggs. She says she works for a master named Vectus. Her master is not who she thinks, and the eggs were wanted for something far worse than science.

entries.title: Dreadmaul Rock
body: A mineral-rich mountain in the east of the Burning Steppes, riddled with caves and mines, held by the Firegut ogres. The ogres are allies of the Blackrock orcs and keep its supply lines open for them.

Their leader Krom'Grul holds rituals there. He captured a whole Horde platoon from Kargath and killed every soldier except Sha'ni Proudtusk, whom he saved for the altar. Her ghost waits there for someone to take her wedding ring home to her husband.

entries.title: Blackrock Stronghold
body: The orcish fortress of the Blackrock clan at the foot of Blackrock Mountain, guarding the road into the spire. It was from here that the orcs raided Redridge.

The Firegut brute lord Gor'tesh ruled from a Blackrock building to the west of Dreadmaul Rock rather than from his own mountain. His head ended up on a pike at the top of it, to the ogres' great dismay.

entries.title: The Ruins of Thaurissan
body: The ruins of the Dark Iron city that Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan founded after the War of the Three Hammers, shattered by the explosion that came with Ragnaros. Thaurissan's spies and agents still prowl it.

Treasure hunters come looking for the Tablet of the Seven, which records the knowledge of seven ancient dwarves of great power. Maxwort Uberglint says plainly why he wants it: knowledge and power lead to wealth.
sources: page text 1914 (War of the Three Hammers)

entries.title: Draco'dar and the Dragonkin
body: The south of the Burning Steppes belongs to the black dragonflight. Broodlings, dragonspawn, wyrmkin and drakes nest around Draco'dar and along the Terror Wing Path, and they guard the land below Morgan's Vigil.
The Alliance scouts who watched them reached an uncomfortable conclusion. The Blackrock orcs are not only driven by bloodlust: the black dragons control them, and feed their rage and hostility.

entries.title: The Altar of Storms
body: An old ritual site in the north-west of the Burning Steppes, near Blackrock Mountain. During the Second War, Gul'dan's Shadow Council worked its darkest magic here, raising the first death knights from the bodies of the slain.
Ogres and fire elementals haunt the ground around it today.
sources: pre-Cataclysm lore: the Altar of Storms and the first death knights

entries.title: Cyrus Therepentous
body: A being who keeps a lair in the Burning Steppes and calls everyone else a mortal, or an imbecile. He speaks for the black dragonflight, and knows when its agents in the Searing Gorge have been helped.
Only a fool would disturb him, he says. Those who bring him proof of their worth may be found not entirely useless.

entries.title: Franclorn Forgewright
body: The ghost of a Dark Iron dwarf who stands in the Burning Steppes, offering to tell travellers of the Spire and of the Dark Iron.
He was the architect who built Blackrock Spire for his people, before the Blackrock orcs and their dragon masters took it from them.
sources: pre-Cataclysm lore: Franclorn Forgewright, architect of Blackrock Spire

entries.title: The True Masters
body: The scouts of Morgan's Vigil sent word through Lakeshire to King Varian Wrynn: the Blackrock orcs are pawns, and the black dragonflight their masters. If Lakeshire fell to both, Darkshire would follow, then Goldshire, then Stormwind itself.

In the keep, Lady Katrana Prestor, a noblewoman learned in dragons, advised caution, and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon would not send troops on speculation. Instead, he made the messenger an acting deputy of Stormwind and sent them back alone. The marshal at Morgan's Vigil laughed when they arrived.
